brand.name: Dripos
brand.industry: Coffee shop operating system (vertical SaaS + POS hardware)
brand.description: All-in-one software and hardware platform built exclusively for independent coffee shops. Founded as Frostbyte Technologies Inc, headquartered in NYC. Combines POS, online ordering, branded customer app, kiosk, KDS, loyalty, email/SMS marketing, gift cards, payroll, accounting, inventory, scheduling, and team management into one integrated stack. Target operator is independent coffee shops (counter service, drive-thru, coffee truck, kitchen-forward café, kiosk, pop-up/events), typically 1-5 locations with 8+ employees. Sweet-spot customers are drive-thrus (highest margin) and kitchen-forward cafés (larger ticket sizes). Differentiation: coffee-specific workflows (checklists, inventory, payroll tuned for coffee), fully integrated (no stitching tools), 24/7 US-based support. Strong domain authority (DR 72) with earned media coverage; currently #1 for 'coffee shop POS system' / 'coffee shop POS software' / 'coffee POS software.' Strict B2B focus — avoids B2C consumer coffee content entirely.

business_goals.market_positioning: When an independent coffee shop owner or operator is researching POS, operating software, online ordering, payroll, team management, or any component of running a coffee shop — Dripos should appear as the definitive coffee-shop-only all-in-one platform. Win on coffee-specific intent, not broader POS.
target_metrics: AI visibility for coffee-shop-specific POS and operations queries
Share of voice vs Square, Toast, Clover in coffee-shop context (not general POS)
Mentions in 'best software for coffee shops' / 'coffee shop POS' / 'alternatives to Square/Toast/Clover' queries
Visibility across the operator journey: opening a coffee shop → running it → scaling multi-location
business_goals.freeform_notes: Primary audience is independent coffee shop owners/operators only — no B2C consumer content. Sweet-spot buyers are 1-5 locations, 8+ employees, drive-thru or kitchen-forward. Most prospect objections are price, switching fear, and integration gaps (Dripos is intentionally platform-first, limited external integrations). Dripos-specific comparison keywords (dripos vs square / toast / clover) are high-intent and should be surfaced. Use bold, operator-to-operator tone — not generic SaaS. Avoid broad restaurant POS framing; stay in the coffee lane.
